claim: Picasso Museum costs €15 for the permanent collection (€19 with temporary exhibition), with free entry Thursday afternoons, the first Sunday of every month, and four Open Door days, but free tickets still require advance online booking.
quote: Standard admission is €15 for the permanent collection. A combined ticket including the current temporary exhibition is €19. Every Thursday from 16:00 to 19:00 (winter), the first Sunday of every month all day, and four Open Door days. Free tickets still require online booking.

claim: MNAC general admission is €12 (covers permanent collection, temporary exhibitions and rooftop viewpoint), with free entry every Saturday from 3 PM and the first Sunday of each month, reservation required.
quote: The standard ticket costs €12... access to the building, to visit the permanent collection, the temporary exhibitions and the Rooftop Viewpoint. Free: Every Saturday from 3 PM onward; The first Sunday of each month.

claim: Fundació Joan Miró adult admission is €17 online / €18 on-site, reduced €11 online / €12 on-site, with no advertised free public days.
quote: The general adult admission ticket is €18 on-site or €17 online. Reduced prices... €12 on-site or €11 online. The museum does not advertise specific free admission days for the general public.

claim: MACBA (contemporary art museum) adult tickets cost €12, and the museum opens free on Saturdays from around 4 PM.
quote: Adult tickets cost €12... MACBA from 4 PM, both walk-in

claim: The Articket Barcelona costs €38, grants skip-the-line entry to six art museums (Picasso, Miró, MNAC, MACBA, Tàpies, CCCB), is valid 12 months, and saves roughly €35 if all six are visited.
quote: The Articket costs €38 and grants skip-the-line entry to six of Barcelona's best art museums: MACBA, Picasso Museum, Fundació Antoni Tàpies, Fundació Joan Miró, MNAC, and CCCB. Valid for 12 months from first use.

claim: Palau de la Música Catalana guided or audio-guide tours cost €24 and last about 50 minutes, running daily roughly 9:00 a.m.–3:30 p.m.
quote: Guided tours cost EUR 24, and audio guide tours are EUR 24. Guided tours are available in EN/FR/ES or IT with a duration of 50 minutes, running daily from 9:00 a.m. – 3:30 p.m.

claim: A Domènech i Montaner combined pass costs €45, covering the Palau de la Música (audio guide), Hospital de Sant Pau and tapas; Sant Pau alone is €17 (€21 with audio guide).
quote: A Domenech i Montaner Pass is available for EUR 45, which includes the Palau de la Música with audio guide, Hospital de Sant Pau, and tapas... Hospital de Sant Pau separately, admission is EUR 17 for adults without audio guide, or EUR 21 with audio guide.

claim: Tablao Cordobes on Las Ramblas is regarded as Barcelona's top flamenco venue with intimate unamplified performances and dinner packages around €48–€85, while Palau Dalmases offers the most beautiful Baroque setting from €30.
quote: Tablao Cordobes... probably the best Barcelona has to offer... Premium shows with dinner packages €48–€85. Palau Dalmases: Historic Baroque palace from €30 per person.

claim: Palau Dalmases hosts four ~50-55 minute flamenco shows nightly from €30 and is recommended as a more affordable, romantic alternative to the premium tablaos, widely reviewed as worth it.
quote: Tickets at Palau Dalmases start at just €30, and they host four shows a night, each about 50-55 mins long... Palau Dalmases puts on a fantastic show at a great price & it's definitely worth a visit.

claim: The Picasso Museum focuses on Picasso's formative early works and the Las Meninas series rather than famous Cubist pieces, while the Miró Foundation is praised as a complete artistic world of art, Sert architecture, light and views, and MNAC's rooftop terrace offers panoramas across the city.
quote: Picasso Museum: about watching a genius learn... no Guernica or Cubist hits, only early works and the Las Meninas series. Miró Foundation: a complete artistic world: art + architecture + light + views. MNAC... roof terrace for unrivaled panoramas.

claim: Saturday afternoon is the highest-value free window in Barcelona since MNAC opens free from 3 PM and MACBA from 4 PM (both walk-in) and the two venues are ~10 minutes apart on metro line L1/L2.
quote: Saturday afternoon is the highest-value free combo of the week: MNAC opens free from 3 PM and MACBA from 4 PM, both walk-in, and they're 10 minutes apart on metro line L1/L2.
